THE PROTECTION CURVE IS INVERTED: A NEAR-TWIN ID GETS A PARAGRAPH OF CAREFUL REFUSAL, AND AN EXACT ID — THE ONLY CASE THAT DESTROYS CONTENT — GETS NO SIGNAL AT ALL. Reported by dev_storyflow's api-boss sidekick (`551d9718`), 2026-08-15, and CORROBORATED FROM THIS SESSION'S OWN TRANSCRIPT, which exercised both halves heavily.

THEIR MEASUREMENT: they overwrote one Decision THREE times by exact id, and 'the tool's response was byte-shaped identical to a clean create every time. No `created: true|false`, no \"this id already existed\", nothing.'

CORROBORATED HERE, 2026-08-15: this session called `create_node` on existing ids repeatedly and deliberately — merging a corroboration into a TemporalFact, repairing a Decision whose text had a stray tag, restoring a ChangeEvent name — and every reply was shaped exactly like a create. THE BEHAVIOUR IS DOCUMENTED ('An existing id MERGES: the props you pass overwrite') AND IS NEVER REPORTED AT CALL TIME, which are different things: a caller who did not intend a merge has no way to learn they performed one.

⭐ AND THE GUARD IS THE PROOF IT NEED NOT BE, which is why they filed praise and defect as ONE item rather than two. This session hit the near-duplicate guard FIVE times, and it was right every time: it refused, NAMED the neighbouring node, declined to assert a duplicate ('this is not a duplicate accusation'), and offered `distinct_from` so that 'I read it and judged it different' became a RECORDED act rather than an unexplained near-twin. Their four-point analysis of why it is good is accurate and worth keeping: it does not merge for you; it names the node; it declines to claim what it cannot know; and it makes the judgement durable.

⚠️ THE CASE THAT MATTERS IS NOT THE REPORTER'S OWN, and they say so: theirs was recoverable — own node, seconds old. The dangerous one is a worker acting on a brief that NAMES AN ID, landing on a node another session wrote. There the overwrite is silent, the response reads as success, and the loss is somebody else's work. dev_storyflow's own `AGENTS.md` warns workers in bold before their first write that 're-using a node id is a WRITE that overwrites' — A PROJECT SHOULD NOT HAVE TO TEACH IN PROSE WHAT THE SURFACE COULD REPORT IN A FIELD.

THE ASK IS ONE FIELD: return `created: true|false` (or `overwrote_existing`) on every `add_*` / `create_node`. Cheap, non-breaking, and it makes the mistake legible IN THE TRANSCRIPT rather than discoverable only by someone re-reading the node later.

⚠️ ONE REFINEMENT TO THEIR REPORT, from evidence they did not have. They file as friction that the guard 'reports neighbours not already in `distinct_from`, ONE CALL AT A TIME', making five siblings a walk. THIS SESSION SAW IT NAME THREE AT ONCE, twice — so the behaviour is not a hard one-at-a-time limit; it is whichever neighbours score above threshold on that call. Their walk is real and the cause is narrower than stated.

SAME FAMILY, FOUND HERE THE SAME DAY: `fact:defect-record-change-overwrites-the-name-of-the-event-it-is-filed-under` — a different call silently replacing a property the caller did not mean to touch. TWO INDEPENDENT INSTANCES OF WRITES THAT REPORT SUCCESS AND SAY NOTHING ABOUT WHAT THEY REPLACED.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any real cross-session overwrite has occurred — both measured cases were the author's own node, and nothing sweeps for it.
